name: Asylum -- Refugee Status Determination (PIBA RSD Unit)

qualifying_event.description: A person with a well-founded fear of persecution applies to PIBA's RSD Unit (established 2009); complex cases are reviewed by the National Status Granting Body (NSGB, comprising Interior, Justice, and Foreign Affairs representatives) with final approval by the Minister of Interior.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Application at the Border Control Unit (Bnei Brak); online form and mandatory in-person appointment.

requirements.blocker_text: Complex cases must reach NSGB plenary review within 2 months of the applicant's interview, with the Minister of Interior making the final decision.
Well-founded fear of persecution meeting 1951 Refugee Convention grounds, not rejected 'out of hand' for late filing, failed identity verification, or lack of Convention grounds.

Nationals of certain countries (historically Eritrea and Sudan, arriving via Egypt) received renewable 'conditional release visas' every 2-3 months under group protection rather than individual RSD -- a distinct, lower-status mechanism.

outcome.duration_length: no overall processing time limit; appeals must be filed within 30 days of a decision

sources.title: UNHCR Israel -- national RSD procedures: PIBA's RSD Unit (est. 2009) processes applications via four pathways (out-of-hand rejection, safe-country fast-track for Georgia/Ukraine/Russia, PIBA-director summary procedure, and full NSGB/ministerial regular procedure); no overall processing time limit; 30-day appeal window; group protection ('conditional release visas' renewed every 2-3 months) historically applied to Eritrean and Sudanese arrivals via Egypt rather than individual RSD

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Israel). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 sourced (UNHCR's own Israel-specific procedural page), not a fetched gov.il/PIBA text directly. Israel's asylum system is documented by UNHCR and Israeli human-rights organisations (Hotline for Refugees and Migrants) as slow and low-recognition-rate relative to many countries in this dataset -- 'no overall processing time limits exist' per the source, a notably weaker procedural guarantee than, say, Peru's or Latvia's asylum files, which specify concrete maximum timelines. family_can_join/family_can_work are set false as the conservative default (schema requires a boolean) rather than assumed true, since the source's group-protection ('conditional release visa') mechanism for specific nationalities is structurally different from individual RSD and the source did not clearly state family provisions for either track. work_rights while pending was described only for group-protection holders ('informal access to the labour market') rather than confirmed for individual RSD applicants generally -- disclosed as a gap.
